entries.title: Amazon's Prime Air drone service, which operates across 18 sites in 10 US states, is drawing local opposition; its Baton Rouge hub launches ~30 drones per hour (Kris Maher/Wall Street Journal)
Fan fiction website AO3, run by nonprofit Organization for Transformative Works, returns online after a "security incident", ahead of its four-week timeline (Adeel Hassan/New York Times)
London-based Plural raised a €1B fund to back European startups, one of only a handful of European VCs that raised €1B+ in one go, planning to back 30+ startups (Financial Times)
Jensen Huang's resignation causes dismay and disbelief in Taiwan, his birthplace and where he is "the people's dad"; an official expects little impact on TSMC (Li Yuan/New York Times)
Baidu reports Q3 revenue down 1% YOY to ~$4.6B, its sixth straight quarterly sales decline, and net income of ~$210M; AI businesses are now 50%+ of its revenue (Bloomberg)
Apple is launching a video podcasts section on the Apple TV app, initially for developer testing, and plans to increase video podcasts on its Podcasts app (New York Times)
A look at China's push for AI literacy by 2030, as schools adopt AI-focused curricula, classroom cameras, and AI-generated lessons to mitigate teacher shortages (Reuters)
Analysis: global manufacturing, utility, and mining companies have shed $4.2T in market value since June as the AI "picks and shovels" trade swings into reverse (Clara Murray/Financial Times)
Startups unveil plans to develop floating offshore data centers to bypass land and power constraints, while experts warn of challenges like saltwater corrosion (Jackie Snow/Wall Street Journal)
Russia is bringing young foreign influencers to occupied Ukraine, encouraging them to share their highly curated experiences, to legitimize its occupation (Linda Hourani/The Kyiv Independent)
Delhi-based Bharat Semi, which is developing programmable image sensors combining capture, processing, and AI capabilities on a single chip, raised a $24M seed (Jagmeet Singh/TechCrunch)
Zus Health, which is building an AI-native healthcare data platform, raised a $33M Series B led by Drive Capital, bringing its total funding to $100M+ (Heather Landi/Fierce Healthcare)
Copenhagen-based AI accounting software maker Sumary raised a $25M seed led by Singular, taking its total funding to $29.2M after a $4.2M pre-seed in Nov. 2025 (Sofia Chesnokova/Tech Funding News)
Source: Musk will attend this week's APEC summit in Shenzhen, where Trump, Xi, and Putin will meet; many US business leaders may skip over scheduling conflicts (Nikkei Asia)
Tighter AI chip export rules are gaining bipartisan support in Congress, including a bill to block Chinese companies from accessing chips overseas (Financial Times)
